title: Testing Methods Independently
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of testing methods independently and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—testing normal inputs—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study testing methods independently with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you give reusable behavior a clear input/output contract that can be tested independently. In this lesson, focus on testing normal inputs and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect testing normal inputs with testing boundary conditions before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Testing normal inputs
items.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input.

items.title: Testing boundary conditions
items.text: Control flow decides which statements run and how often. Make conditions precise, set clear loop termination conditions, and test zero/one/many-item boundaries to catch off-by-one errors.

items.title: Testing invalid inputs
items.text: Treat console input as untrusted text. Validate format and range before using it, account for token-versus-line reading, and give users a clear way to correct invalid input.

items.title: Understanding method contracts
items.text: A method gives a named contract to a unit of behavior. Keep responsibilities focused, define clear parameter and return types, and test typical, boundary, and invalid cases independently.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Move one responsibility into a method with clear parameters and a return value. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: build the smallest program that demonstrates testing normal inputs. Change one input, predict the result, and add one boundary or invalid case before considering the task complete.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates at least one listed topic from Testing Methods Independently.
The learner states the expected result before running or inspecting the example.
At least one boundary, failure, compatibility, or maintainability consideration is documented where relevant.
hints: Start by identifying the contract or rule behind testing normal inputs.
Reduce the example to the smallest input that makes the behavior visible.
Test one boundary or failure case and compare the result with the expected behavior.
content.execution_notes: Java requires a JDK or a separate isolated server runner. No Java sandbox is bundled with this content; never execute learner code inside the FastAPI process or public production container.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.

summary: Testing Methods Independently is best understood by connecting its contract to a small observable example.
Key syllabus points: Testing normal inputs, Testing boundary conditions, Testing invalid inputs.
Use official versioned documentation and tests to confirm assumptions before relying on behavior in a larger application.
